messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

Then for each event_id, choose the highest visible revision among those kept (the revisions field, likely integer). They replace earlier revisions. Since all revisions are 1, no duplicates; we keep all events with received_time <= 100.

Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time (target_time = 100). Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. The known events happen up to target_time=100, which includes all events up to event_time <= 100. All events are <=100 (max event_time in report is 99). So all events will be included.

The historical reconstruction will produce:

- stock_at_target: stock after processing up to target_time.

Then apply future_schedule: Starting from the stock after target_time (stock_at_target). Apply events in (event_time, event_id) order (by event_time, then event_id sorting). This will result in final stock after horizon_time (which is 130) after processing events up to horizon_time (including events up to horizon_time inclusive). However, note that horizon_time in input is 130; future_schedule includes events up to event_time = 130. So after processing all future events, we have stock_at_horizon.

We need also future_lost: total lost sales from processing only the future_schedule events (i.e., only for events after target_time). Actually the problem says: "After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future. Return ... future_lost for the scenario ONLY". So that means lost sales from future events only (i.e., ignore any lost sales from historical events). It's lost sales due to demands in future_schedule.

Also first_future_stockout_time: the earliest event_time among future events that had unmet demand (stockout). If no unmet demand, -1.

We must ignore stockout events from historical events for first_future_stockout_time.
